concepts.title: Convex polytopes: V- and H-representations
concepts.blurb: A convex polytope is at once the convex hull of finitely many vertices (V-representation) and a bounded intersection of half-spaces (H-representation); the Minkowski–Weyl theorem says these two descriptions coincide, and the faces of a polytope organize into the face lattice.

concepts.title: Faces & the Euler relation
concepts.blurb: The f-vector records how many faces a polytope has in each dimension, and the Euler–Poincaré relation Σ(−1)ⁱ fᵢ = 1−(−1)ᵈ ties these counts together — specializing to V−E+F = 2 for 3-dimensional polytopes.

concepts.title: Pick's theorem
concepts.blurb: For a lattice polygon, Pick's theorem computes the area as I + B/2 − 1 from the interior and boundary lattice-point counts — a self-contained two-dimensional miracle that turns out to be the d = 2 case of Ehrhart theory.

concepts.title: The Ehrhart polynomial
concepts.blurb: For a lattice d-polytope P, the lattice-point count L_P(t) = #(tP ∩ ℤᵈ) of the t-fold dilate is a degree-d polynomial in t, with leading coefficient the volume of P and constant term 1.

concepts.title: Ehrhart–Macdonald reciprocity
concepts.blurb: Evaluating the Ehrhart polynomial at negative integers counts interior lattice points: (−1)ᵈ L_P(−t) = L_{P°}(t), Macdonald's reciprocity law relating the closed polytope to its interior.

concepts.title: The Ehrhart series & h*-vector
concepts.blurb: Packaging the Ehrhart polynomial into a generating function gives Σ L_P(t) zᵗ = h*(z)/(1−z)^{d+1}; Stanley's nonnegativity theorem makes the h*-vector a sequence of nonnegative integers summing to the normalized volume d!·vol(P).
